ref: Diagnose probable aphthous ulcer (mouth symptoms page)
text: Evidence is the bare 'Ulcer of mouth' (disorder), so every mouth ulcer and every descendant (traumatic, drug-induced, thermal/chemical burn ulceration, recurrent ulcer) yields a probable aphthous ulcer. The page's discriminators 'painful' and 'with central white patch' are lost. This is the one probable rule on the page whose trigger is materially broader than the page.

The approach box says 'If on abacavir, check for abacavir hypersensitivity reaction (AHR) 131'. By the house standard this is a 'consider X' and should be a possible rule triggered by mouth symptoms plus abacavir exposure, the same pre-screen pattern used for anaphylaxis in this file. 'Abacavir' (substance) and 'Hypersensitivity to abacavir' / 'Allergy to abacavir' (finding) exist in SNOMED; whether a finding-category concept is accepted as a diagnosis would need confirming. No rule or check_for item exists for it.

ref: Diagnose probable angular cheilitis / impetigo around the mouth / contact dermatitis at corners of mouth
text: All three share the fissure trigger with no exclusions, so a patient with cracked corners plus perioral crusts and blisters receives probable angular cheilitis AND probable impetigo, and one with severe itching receives probable angular cheilitis AND probable contact dermatitis. The page frames impetigo and contact dermatitis as alternative conclusions ('If crusts and blisters ... impetigo likely', 'If very itchy, contact dermatitis likely'). The language has (not ...) to express the exclusion. Reasonable people could leave this as is.

ref: Urgent: mouth symptoms with inability to open mouth or anaphylaxis signs; Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from mouth symptoms
text: 'Mouth symptoms' (finding) is the due_to of both tasks and a conjunct in the priority evaluation and the possible rule, but it is not checked for anywhere in this file and is not among the listed common symptoms or warning signs. Test constraint 5 (every priority-evaluation evidence must be checked for in the same file, or be a vital/warning sign/common symptom/probable active_condition) may reject it unless another page records it; the house brief's own pattern '(and <presenting complaint> (or ...))' invites exactly this, so this may be a known, accepted gap. Cannot verify without the VHA repo.

ref: Diagnose probable impetigo around the mouth
text: Requires angle-of-mouth fissure AND crust AND blister. Page says only 'crusts and blisters around mouth' for impetigo. Impetigo cannot fire from perioral crusts/blisters alone.
Triggered by any Ulcer of mouth; the page's branch is a painful ulcer with a central white patch. Over-fires.

ref: Diagnose probable contact dermatitis at corners of mouth
text: Requires fissure; page says only 'very itchy'. Under-fires.
Allergen exposure has no recency (past few hours), and 'Insect bite - wound' is a loose concept for exposure to possible allergen. Over-fires for Urgent.
Hard-requires white patches in mouth; the page only requires difficulty or pain on swallowing.

Two check_for items (Itching severe, Crust, Blister perioral) are fine, but 'Weight decreased' etc. exist only to support the diabetes rule; there is no check/diagnosis for oral candida within dry mouth or medication-induced dry mouth.
